data.title: UK Stock Market Today: FTSE 100 Futures Drop On Stronger Dollar And Fed Rate Fears
data.description:
The Morning Bull - UK Market Morning Update Friday, 20 Nov 2026

UK stocks look set for a weaker open, with FTSE 100 futures pointing lower as a resurgent dollar dominates sentiment. The British pound trading near a 51-week low around 1.31 against the dollar reinforces that cautious tone.

Fresh Federal Reserve minutes have strengthened expectations of further US rate hikes, and the US 10-year yield is around 5.05%. That combination supports the dollar and weighs on global equities, which is feeding directly into UK futures this morning.

A softer pound can offer some earnings relief for internationally focused UK businesses when they translate overseas revenue back into sterling. Higher US yields at the same time keep global borrowing costs under pressure, which can challenge more indebted firms and rate-sensitive pockets of the UK market.

The open now hinges on whether today’s UK retail sales data validates the cautious global mood or pushes back against it. If domestic demand looks firmer than expected, investors face a trade-off between weaker global risk appetite and a still resilient UK consumer backdrop.

Stocks to Watch Before the Opening Bell

Marks and Spencer Group (MKS)

Marks and Spencer Group is pushing deeper into Asia Pacific through a partnership with Global Fashion Group. Shoppers in Southeast Asia can already buy M&S products on ZALORA. Australia and New Zealand are set to follow on THE ICONIC in early 2027. Centralised storage in Kuala Lumpur aims to speed up delivery and support online demand.

AstraZeneca (AZN)

AstraZeneca is in focus after a series of drug pipeline and partnership headlines. A US Priority Review for sonesitatug vedotin in advanced gastric and related cancers highlights regulatory momentum, with a decision expected in the second quarter of 2027. New lupus research collaboration work and fresh competition in myasthenia gravis treatments add moving parts around its immunology franchise.

Pan African Resources (PAF)

Pan African Resources has confirmed a final dividend of 65.00000 ZA cents per share for the year to 30 June 2026, following shareholder approval at the AGM where all but one resolution passed. Management has set out payment dates and FX rates for conversions into £, US$, and A$, so income focused investors may want to check currency details.

Top Movers

  • Babcock International Group (LSE:BAB) jumped 9.38% after reporting 13% underlying profit growth and lifting its interim dividend.
  • EnQuest (LSE:ENQ) climbed 6.80% on its North Sea asset sale plan and an analyst upgrade to Buy with target.
  • Avacta Group (AIM:AVCT) gained 6.51% after new AVA6207 preclinical data showed activity in resistant tumor models and synthetic lethality.

Top Losers

  • PayPoint (LSE:PAY) fell 21.96% after half-year profit and parcel net revenue both came in lower.
  • Beauty Tech Group (LSE:TBTG) declined 8.99% after Thakral Corporation exited its stake through an accelerated secondary placing.
  • Close Brothers Group (LSE:CBG) dropped 7.73% as shares reacted to a revised cost outlook and sector-specific pressures.

On The Radar

UK data and a packed run of domestic earnings sit alongside US rate signals, putting the focus squarely on how the FTSE 100 handles a firm dollar and mixed consumer momentum.

  • UK Retail Sales MoM, Fri 20 Nov. The consensus sits at 0% after a 0.4% decline last month. Any clear beat would underline consumer resilience and can support UK focused retailers, while a weaker print keeps pressure on growth sensitive stocks.
  • UK Retail Sales YoY, Fri 20 Nov. Annual sales are forecast around 1.2% versus 0.8% previously. A result well above that band would speak to volume demand helping listed supermarkets and general retailers absorb higher financing and wage costs.
  • UK CBI Industrial Trends Orders, Fri 20 Nov. The November reading is projected near minus 30 versus minus 32. A softer outcome would highlight export and manufacturing strain that often weighs on mid cap cyclicals and sterling together.
  • easyJet, Wed 25 Nov. Full year 2026 results put guidance and unit revenue in the spotlight. Any shift in booking trends feeds directly into how investors think about demand sensitive UK travel and leisure shares.
  • Compass Group, Tue 24 Nov. Fiscal 2026 numbers at 7:00 AM focus attention on margin performance and contract wins in catering, which matter for how the market prices steady cash generators inside the FTSE 100.

Sector & Industry Watch

Materials and Metals and Mining: Steep pullback after strong year

Materials and Metals and Mining have had the sharpest weekly setback, with both groups giving up around 10% after a solid 12 month run. Pressure on stocks such as Rio Tinto, which dropped about 8.8%, lines up with weaker commodity prices and softer sentiment toward resource heavy sectors.

For anyone holding big miners and materials producers, today’s UK CBI Industrial Trends Orders print is the key check because a weak factory order backdrop would underline concerns about real economy demand for metals.

Energy and Oil and Gas: Softer week as crude stays subdued

Energy and Oil and Gas are down over the past seven days and over the month while still ahead over the year. The retreat comes as Brent trades near three month lows around US$83 a barrel, which squeezes revenue expectations for producers even though the sector trades on relatively low P/E multiples compared with its own history.

If you hold UK oil stocks, the swing factor now is how crude reacts to ongoing US rate expectations and the latest global inventory signals because any further pressure on prices would keep the recent sector drift in focus.

Financials and Banks: Rate sensitive group under pressure

Financials have slipped around 4% over the week, with Banks weaker still and shares such as HSBC and Close Brothers both under strain. Higher global yields and cautious equity markets raise questions about loan growth, bad debts and fee income at a time when valuations for the sector are already close to recent norms.

The data point to watch is today’s UK GfK Consumer Confidence reading because a softer household mood often feeds into slower credit demand and more caution around borrowing, which matters directly for high street lenders and broader Financials.

Healthcare and Pharmaceuticals & Biotech: Regulatory news meets share pullback

Healthcare and Pharmaceuticals & Biotech have eased over the past week even though recent headlines for AstraZeneca, Scancell and IXICO highlight active drug and tools pipelines. Investors are weighing long term potential, such as FDA Priority Review for new cancer therapies, against current share price weakness and sector valuations around 22x P/E that sit slightly below three year averages.

If you hold Healthcare funds or individual drug makers, the main catalyst to monitor is upcoming US and UK regulatory milestones on key programmes because clear progress or setbacks on approvals can quickly shift sentiment for this whole group.

Tech and Semiconductors: Hot AI theme cools after strong run

Tech has slipped over the past week, and Semiconductors have fallen even more after a very large 12 month gain of around 7x for the industry. Enthusiasm around AI hardware and software, underlined by events such as the Anthropic IPO, now meets profit taking and concern that earlier expectations for future earnings may have moved too far ahead of underlying revenues.

For UK investors exposed to Tech and chip related stocks, the next major signal comes from early reads on global IT spending in trading updates, since any sign that corporate customers are slowing cloud or AI infrastructure projects would test the sector’s recent premium pricing.
